summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style article on the Lincoln Town Car, a full-size luxury sedan marketed by Ford's Lincoln division from 1981 to 2011. It explains the name's origin in a limousine style and the nameplate's history as a Continental sub-model from 1959 and later a trim line. It also gives an overview table covering production years, platform, related models and succession.
one_line: The Lincoln Town Car was a full-size luxury sedan sold by Ford's Lincoln division from 1981 to 2011.
key_facts: The Lincoln Town Car is a model line of full-size luxury sedans marketed by the Lincoln division of Ford Motor Company from 1981 to 2011.
The name Town Car derives from a style of limousine.
The French term for Town Car is 'Sedan de Ville'.
The Cadillac rival to the Lincoln Continental from the 1950s to the 1990s was the Sedan de Ville.
The Town Car nameplate first appeared as a sub-model of the Continental in 1959.
The Town Car later became a trim line during the 1970s.
For 1981, the Lincoln Town Car became a distinct product, taking the place of the previous Continental in the Lincoln model line.
The Lincoln Town Car's production ran from 1980 to 2011.
The Lincoln Town Car's model years were 1981 to 2011.
The Lincoln Town Car was classified as a full-size luxury car (F) with an FR layout.
The Lincoln Town Car used the Ford Panther platform.
The Mercury Grand Marquis and Ford Crown Victoria were related models to the Lincoln Town Car.
The predecessor of the Lincoln Town Car was the Lincoln Continental (1980).
The successors listed for the Lincoln Town Car were the Lincoln MKS (full-size sedan) and the Lincoln Continental (2017).
